# #43, one lemma: the Coble cusp image is the $\delta$-preserving part of Sterk's $G_v$, and its orbits number two

**Lemma.** At `(4.3.9)` the image of the Coble cusp stabilizer in $O(K_I)$ is the subgroup of Sterk's $G_v$ generated by
the chamber's reflections and the one diagram symmetry that fixes $\delta$; its orbits on the three root classes are
$\\{\alpha_{12}\\}$ and $\{\alpha_{13},\alpha_{14}\}$, so the Coble count at that cusp is $2$.

**Argument.** Two halves, one from the printed page and one computed.

*The printed half.* Sterk states the structure of the cusp image at `(4.3.7)`, p. 22: "$G_v = \{\pm1\}W_v \rtimes
\mathbb{Z}/2$", and at `(4.3.9)`, p. 24, that "Symmetries of the graph can be lifted to $\Gamma_v$" — the same
statement, with the reflection subgroup $W_v$ supplying the rest. So $G_v$ is generated by the reflections in the
chamber's walls and the diagram's symmetries. The stored $T_{En}$ row at `lattices/029J.md:524` rests on exactly this:
the eight symmetries act transitively on $\alpha_{11},\alpha_{12},\alpha_{13},\alpha_{14}$, so the image has one orbit,
and the row says one.

*The computed half.* Of the eight symmetries, exactly two carry $\delta$ to $\pm\delta$ — the identity and the one
exchanging $\alpha_{13}$ with $\alpha_{14}$ and fixing $\alpha_{11}$, $\alpha_{12}$ — and every reflection in a wall of
$T_{\mathrm{Co}}$ fixes $\delta$ (`results/issue-43-lemma-reflections-fix-delta.md`). So the $\delta$-preserving part of
$G_v$ is $\langle W_v, \sigma\rangle$, whose orbits on $\{\alpha_{12},\alpha_{13},\alpha_{14}\}$ are
$\{\alpha_{12}\}$ and $\{\alpha_{13},\alpha_{14}\}$ — two orbits. $\square$

**What the lemma rests on, stated plainly.** It assumes that the Coble cusp stabilizer's image is the $\delta$-preserving
*subgroup* of Sterk's $G_v$, i.e. that no element of $\Gamma_{\mathrm{En},2}$ outside $\langle W_v, S\rangle$ preserves
$\delta$ and moves a class. Sterk asserts the shape of $G_v$ at (4.3.7) and asserts the symmetries lift at (4.3.9); he
does not assert that $G_v$ is *only* reflections and symmetries at (4.3.9), and no printed source in this repository
does. The 029J rows make the same assumption in the other direction — they read the image as the whole of $G_v$ — and
they are stored. That is why the count of $2$ is recorded as a lemma and not as a row: the issue's rule is that a value
is cited or certified, and this one is neither while the assumption is open.

**What would close it.** Either a printed statement that $G_v = \{\pm 1\}W_v \rtimes S_v$ at `(4.3.9)` — Sterk gives it
only at `(4.3.7)` — or an exhibited element of $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Co},2}$ carrying $\alpha_{12}$ to the other two, which
would make the count $1$ and refute the lemma's numerical claim while leaving its structural content intact.

**Sources by printed page.** H. Sterk, *Compactifications of the period space of Enriques surfaces, Part I*,
Math. Z. 207 (1991), 1–36: `(4.3.7)`, p. 22, for $G_v = \{\pm1\}W_v \rtimes \mathbb{Z}/2$; `(4.3.9)`, p. 24, for the
lifting of the symmetries; `(4.3.10)`, p. 25, for the span $\mathbb{Z}\{e-f,e+f\}\oplus E_8(-2)$ that contains
$\delta$. The wall data and the symmetry computation are card 029J's.
